test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 4 March 2023)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a measure of relative dispersion?
solution:
The correct answer is the **coefficient of variation. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Coefficient of variation: **

The coefficient of variation (CV) is a statistical measure that expresses the standard deviation as a percentage of the mean. It is calculated by dividing the standard deviation by the mean and multiplying by 100. The CV provides a relative measure of dispersion because it considers the standard deviation in relation to the mean. It is commonly used when comparing the variability of different datasets with different means. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Quartile deviation: **The quartile deviation measures the spread or dispersion of a dataset by calculating the difference between the upper quartile (Q3) and the lower quartile (Q1). However, it does not provide a relative measure of dispersion since it is an absolute measure that does not take into account the magnitude of the data values.
 
• **Harmonic mean:** The harmonic mean is a measure of central tendency and does not directly measure dispersion. It calculates the reciprocal of the average of the reciprocals of a set of values. It is primarily used to calculate rates or averages in cases where the data values have a reciprocal relationship, such as rates of speed or time.
 
• **Standard deviation: **The standard deviation is a measure of dispersion that quantifies the amount of variation or spread in a dataset. It measures the average distance of data points from the mean. While the standard deviation provides an absolute measure of dispersion, it does not directly provide a relative measure unless it is compared to the mean or other reference values.

**Hence the coefficient of variation is the measure of relative dispersion.**
